solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Final stage of house extension

parts.note: a house is a home
an extension of something is a stretch of it

explanation.surface: The last phase of building an addition to a house.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a building project; 'house' and 'extension' each give one half of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The run-in to the finishing post on a racecourse, figuratively the closing phase of any effort.

clue.text: Receiver's needed for dates he organised

indicators.note: organised means the letters of the words before it are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A telephone receiver is wanted so that he can arrange his dates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges DATES HE; ''s needed for' only joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A headset is a set of earphones, a device that receives sound signals.

clue.text: Mongrel will get no flipping meat

parts.note: a mongrel dog is a mutt

indicators.note: flipping means the little word no is turned over and read the other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mongrel dog won't get any of the blasted meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British swear word qualifying 'meat', but it turns NO into ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The flesh of a grown sheep, eaten as food, is a kind of meat.

clue.text: Mediocre time comes with cost

parts.note: a second is a unit of time
a rate is a price or charge, a cost

explanation.surface: Time spent with a price attached proves only so-so.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of inferior quality, not top class, is ordinary or mediocre.

clue.text: Run on the bank, that's growing

definitions.meaning: a marsh plant with tall stems found at the water's edge

explanation.surface: Something running along a riverbank and flourishing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition describes the waterside plant; the comma splits the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means hurry; as a noun it is a reed-like plant of riverbanks.

clue.text: Current flowing across river near equator

indicators.note: flowing across means the first piece spreads round the second, holding it inside

parts.note: current events are topical ones

explanation.surface: An ocean current runs over a river close to the equator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like a noun about water but is the adjective meaning up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics are the regions lying on either side of the equator.

clue.text: Another thing about this gauge of model railway is sounding the horn

indicators.note: about means the rearranged word goes round the gauge letters
another version of a word is a remade arrangement of its letters

parts.note: OO is a common scale of model railway

explanation.surface: Another item concerning a model-railway gauge is the sound of a horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' rearranges the letters of 'thing' to HTING, and 'about' wraps that round the OO gauge, a common British model-railway scale.
explanation.definitionFit: A car or owl producing a hoot is honking, the noise of a horn being sounded.

clue.text: Carts I'd overturned — that's radical

indicators.note: overturned means the letters are upset and fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Tipping over the carts was an extreme step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' suggests a straight reversal, but that gives DISTRAC; the letters are rearranged instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A drastic measure is extreme and far-reaching, synonym of a radical one.

clue.text: Deduce side from which kings took authority

parts.note: to divine something is to work it out or deduce it
the right is one side

explanation.surface: A ruler infers which side supported royal power.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctrine claimed monarchs got their power directly from God.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctrine that monarchs rule by God's will was the source of royal authority.

clue.text: Don't go on to break one's journey

definitions.meaning: to halt and get off rather than carry on
to make a short halt during travel

explanation.surface: Stay put rather than carry on, to interrupt a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief halt on the way somewhere is a break in a journey.

clue.text: One has to take hurried steps in it

definitions.text: One has to take hurried steps in it

parts.words: One has to take hurried steps in it
parts.note: the soldier on a fast long-distance military route must step quickly

explanation.surface: Something that makes you rush your steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A military march at speed over a long distance, where troops step out quickly.

clue.text: Peer is number five to start

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
taken as written
a count is a number or total

explanation.surface: A lord says he is number five in the starting line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start' puts V at the front of the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscount is a rank in the British peerage, between earl and baron.

clue.text: I had to break up row, being smarter

indicators.note: to break up means the row is split open to hold another piece

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
I'd, written ID, is short for I had

explanation.surface: I had to stop a quarrel, and came off looking better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidier means neater or more well-kept, which is what smarter means here.

clue.text: Brief note written out in full

definitions.text: Brief note written out in full

parts.words: Brief note written out in full
parts.note: a short note's clipped name, memo, expanded to its full form

explanation.surface: A short message given at length.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo is the abbreviated word; the full word names the same written message.

clue.text: Some estaminet takings may be after tax

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a small French café's revenue may be counted after tax.
explanation.walkthrough: An estaminet is a small French bar or café.
explanation.definitionFit: Nett income is what remains once deductions such as tax are taken off.

clue.text: Primitive plants developed from a large gene

indicators.note: developed means these letters grow into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Simple plants evolved from one big gene.
explanation.definitionFit: Green algae are simple chlorophyll-bearing organisms, among the earliest plant life.

clue.text: Pantomime involved notepaper — nothing was left out

indicators.note: involved means the letters are tangled up into a new order
was left out means the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Christmas show involved writing paper, nothing omitted.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O from NOTEPAPER to get NTEPAPER, then 'involved' rearranges it. A pantomime is a British family Christmas stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: The boy who never grows up is the hero of a famous Christmas stage show staged as a pantomime.

clue.text: Making one more time for fun

explanation.surface: Building something again for amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: Read with a hyphen it is making anew; as one word it is leisure enjoyment.

clue.text: Way amateur infuses part of milk to produce sauce

indicators.note: infuses means these pieces are steeped inside the milk word

parts.note: curd is the solid part of soured milk
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A novice cook steeps milk to make a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Custard is a sweet sauce of milk and eggs poured over puddings in Britain.

clue.text: Clear off, having mislaid right racket

indicators.note: having mislaid means a letter has been lost from the word

parts.note: scram means clear off, go away

explanation.surface: Get out, having lost a decent tennis racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' suggests sport but means a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a dishonest scheme, which a scam is.

clue.text: Hun cut short invading borders of Cathay, with a show of spite

indicators.note: invading means the trimmed piece pushes inside the border letters
borders of means the first and last letters of the word
cut short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: Attila was king of the Huns

explanation.surface: A Hun, stopped early, invading the edges of China, acting spitefully.
explanation.walkthrough: Cathay is an old name for China, fitting the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting catty is being spiteful; the adverb means in a spiteful manner.

clue.text: Ice in French or Norwegian port

parts.note: a berg is a mass of floating ice
en is French for in

explanation.surface: Ice found in a French or Norwegian harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bergen is a city and harbour on Norway's west coast.

clue.text: Mark's kind of music?

definitions.meaning: the book of the evangelist Mark in the New Testament
a style of Christian vocal music

explanation.surface: Asking what genre a man called Mark likes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark's account of Jesus is one of the four New Testament books; it is also a music genre.

clue.text: Better fiddle gas meter!

indicators.note: fiddle means the letters are tampered with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Cheat by tampering with the gas meter!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like an adjective but is one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler is one who bets, so a better in the wagering sense.

clue.text: Real torture at intervals

indicators.note: at intervals means every other letter is taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Genuine torture, inflicted now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Something genuine or actual is real, a synonym.

clue.text: Person seeking fur — salesman getting some returned

indicators.note: returned means the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
part means some of something

explanation.surface: A fur hunter and a salesman getting some goods sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses both REP and PART together.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapper catches animals for their pelts, so he is after fur.

clue.text: Shark needs to follow trawl

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them
to trawl is to fish with a net

explanation.surface: A shark must trail the fishing net.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogfish is a small shark common in British waters.

clue.text: Risk capital

parts.note: money invested in a venture, read instead as payment for running a risk

explanation.surface: Funds invested in a speculative venture.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra pay for hazardous work is cash earned because of peril.
